title: Manager, Sales Development, EMEA
description:
WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth - personal, professional, and financial - is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission - operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today - and we’re just getting started.

ROLE OVERVIEW

Harvey is looking for a driven, strategic, and entrepreneurial Sales Development Manager to lead and scale our SDR team across EMEA. This will be the first dedicated SDR leadership role in the region, responsible for building a high-performing team that generates pipeline across leading law firms, professional services organizations, and in-house legal teams.

You will own hiring, onboarding, coaching, and performance management while partnering closely with Sales, Marketing, and RevOps to build a scalable pipeline generation engine. You’ll also help shape Harvey’s regional go-to-market strategy by refining targeting, messaging, and outbound programs that resonate with the European legal market.

If you’re excited by the idea of building teams, developing talent, and driving impact at a fast-growing AI company transforming legal work, we’d love to meet you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own regional pipeline performance: Drive the SDR team’s contribution to pipeline generation across inbound and outbound channels, ensuring strong alignment with EMEA sales targets.

- Build and scale the team: Hire, onboard, and develop a high-performing SDR team, helping establish the structure, operating cadence, and performance standards for the EMEA region.

- Coach and develop SDRs: Deliver hands-on coaching through regular 1:1s, call reviews, and deal strategy sessions to accelerate rep development and performance.

- Design onboarding and enablement: Partner with GTM enablement to create onboarding and ongoing training programs that ramp SDRs quickly and build strong product, industry, and prospecting expertise.

- Partner cross-functionally: Collaborate closely with Sales, Marketing, and RevOps to improve lead routing, campaign effectiveness, and pipeline conversion.

- Refine targeting and messaging: Continuously test and improve outbound strategies, messaging, and account targeting based on ICP fit and performance insights.

- Leverage data and tools: Use platforms such as Salesforce, Salesloft, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Gong, and ZoomInfo to track team performance and optimize workflows.

- Build a strong team culture: Foster a high-performance culture grounded in ownership, learning, and collaboration.

WHAT YOU HAVE

- 4+ years of experience in SaaS sales or business development, with at least 1-2 years of direct SDR or BDR leadership experience.

- Proven success in building and managing pipeline-generating teams in a high-growth, outbound-focused environment.

- Deep understanding of modern sales development tools (e.g., Salesforce, Salesloft, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Gong).

- A data-driven mindset with the ability to analyze team performance, uncover insights, and iterate quickly.

- Experience building SDR processes from scratch-comf

title: Expert Data Modeler, Fraud Risk Detection
description:
Overview
Experian 's Fraud Analytics & Commercialization operates across four main functions. These include client engagement analytics, scalable and custom analytics for financial institutions, fraud analytics consulting, and solution integrity and enablement for production-ready platforms.
We're looking for a motivated Data Scientist to help build fraud detection models and features that identify high-risk activity while minimizing friction for legitimate customers. Core skills for this role include an eagerness to collaborate, and empathy. You will will dig into surprising signals in the data and to learn how that insight becomes a deployed model.
You will help investigate the latest fraud patterns, build features, and train and evaluate machine learning models. You will work with senior data scientists and engineers starting with problem definition through feature engineering, experimentation, and deployment. You will be a developing programmer, ready to translate theoretical principles into production-ready solutions.
We continue to sharpen through research and the engineering that turns those findings into tools and systems built for commercialization.
This is a remote role and you will report into the Sr. Manager of Fraud Analytics.
What you'll do

• Investigate large datasets, including exploratory analysis and fraud label development, to identify latest fraud patterns, attack methods, and behavioral signals.

• Translate ambiguous fraud and risk problems into clear hypotheses, analytical plans, model requirements, and measurable success criteria.

• Develop machine learning models for fraud detection across account opening, account takeover, and identity risk.

• Evaluate models using metrics like ROC/AUC/KS/Gini, precision/recall, fraud capture rate, false-positive rate, customer friction, and fraud losses prevented.

• Develop and validate predictive features using identity, transactional, consumer credit history, device, behavioral, temporal, velocity, network, and third-party data.

• Write clean, efficient, well-tested Python and PySpark code, and collaborate with teams to bring models and features into batch, retro, or real-time decisioning environments.

• Monitor feature quality, model performance, population changes, and fraud-pattern drift

• Design and present analyses for model behavior, tradeoffs, risks, and recommendations

• Follow appropriate standards for data privacy, model documentation, explainability, validation, and governance.

Qualifications

• At least 3 years of experience in data science, machine learning, statistical modeling, or a related quantitative field

• Bachelor's or advanced degree in computer science, statistics, engineering, data science, or another quantitative discipline

• Direct experience developing fraud-detection, identity-risk, credit-risk, financial-crime, or other adversarial risk models.

• Demonstrated experience creating meaningful fraud features

• Proficiency in Python and PySpark, with experience writing modular and tested code for large datasets and distributed or cloud data systems.

• Experience using common data science and machine-learning tools such as pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, XGBoost, TensorFlow, or comparable technologies.

• Knowledge of supervised learning, model evaluation, feature selection, statistical inference, experimentation, and model calibration.

• Experience navigating challenges common to fraud modeling, including class imbalance, delayed or incomplete labels, changing attack patterns, and model drift.

• Experience moving models beyond experimentation and into production, either directly or in close partnership with engineering teams.

Benefits/Perks:

• Great compensation package and bonus plan

• Core benefits including medical, dental, vision, and matching 401K

• Flexible work environment, ability to work remote, hybrid or in-office

• Flexible time off including volunteer time off, vacation, sick and 12-paid holidays

title: Product Manager - QA & Release Coordination (AI x Greentech) (m/f/d)
description:
As a Product Manager at Reonic, you’ll sit at the intersection of product, engineering, and our customers.

You’ll help make sure new features are tested thoroughly, releases run smoothly, and customer feedback continuously makes its way back into the product development process.

You’ll have a lot of ownership and work closely with engineers and other teams to improve both our product and the way we build and release it.

Please note: This is a fully onsite role in Augsburg.

What you'll do

- Own release testing: Coordinate testing for upcoming releases and continuously test new features during development. Identify issues early and provide clear, actionable feedback to engineering.

- Coordinate software releases: Keep track of features, changes, dependencies, and release timelines. Act as a communication hub between product, engineering, and other teams.

- Improve product quality: Look beyond whether a feature technically works. Think about edge cases, usability, customer workflows, and how changes affect the overall product experience.

- Turn feedback into action: Triage user feedback and bug reports, investigate issues, reproduce problems, and translate findings into clear, well-described tickets for engineering.

- Communicate what's new: Create release notes, run internal demos, and make sure colleagues understand what has changed and how new functionality works.

- Work closely with engineering: Collaborate with engineers throughout the development process, ask the right questions, and help remove ambiguity before features reach customers.

- Understand our customers: Build a deep understanding of the businesses using Reonic and use that context to make better product decisions.

What Makes You a Great Fit

- Product mindset: You naturally think beyond checklists. You want to understand why something is being built, who it is for, and what makes it useful.

- Attention to detail: You spot inconsistencies, edge cases, and potential issues before they become customer problems.

- Strong communication: You can clearly communicate with engineers, product colleagues, and other stakeholders. Professional fluency in English (C1+) is required.

- Technical curiosity: You enjoy understanding how software works and aren't afraid to dig into technical details, investigate bugs, or learn new concepts.

- Customer orientation: You care about the experience of the people using the product and can turn qualitative feedback into actionable insights.

- Ownership: You take responsibility, follow things through, and don't wait for someone else to solve a problem that you can help solve yourself.

- Startup mindset: You’re comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve and processes are still being built.

- Relevant experience: Experience in product management, product operations, QA, software development, B2B SaaS, or a similar role is a plus. A degree in economics, engineering, computer science, or a related field is also helpful, but not required.

Why Join Us?

- Real impact: Help build software that enables businesses to accelerate the transition to renewable energy.

- A product people use: Our platform is already used by 3,000+ paying B2B customers, giving you the opportunity to work on a product with real users and real-world impact.

- High ownership: We’re a growing company, and nothing is set in stone. You’ll have plenty of room to shape how we work and how the product evolves.

- Fast-moving environment: Work closely with engineering and other teams, make decisions quickly, and see your work reach customers.

- A great international team: We work hard, learn from each other, and make sure we have fun along the way.

- Great setup: MacBook, gym membership subsidy, regular team events, coffee, Deutschland ticket and other perks.

- Competitive compensation: We offer competitive pay based on your experience and responsibilities.

Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply! I

title: Head of Delivery
description:
WHO WE ARE

Roboflow is on a mission to give software the sense of sight.

Our platform makes it easier for developers and organizations to build, deploy, and manage computer vision applications. More than 1 million developers have used Roboflow, and our customers range from startups to some of the largest companies in the world.

As computer vision moves from experimentation into production, we're helping companies deploy visual AI into the physical world - across manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, retail, and countless other industries.

We're looking for a Head of Delivery to own and scale how we take our most complex customers from vision to production.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Our customers come to Roboflow with ambitious problems: automating quality inspection, monitoring infrastructure, understanding physical environments, improving operational workflows, and building entirely new products powered by computer vision.

Getting those applications into production often requires much more than handing a customer software.

Our Delivery organization, including Implementation Engineering and Forward Deployed Engineering, works alongside customers to turn those ideas into real, production-ready systems.

We're looking for a leader who can build this function for the next stage of Roboflow's growth.

You'll own the teams, operating model, and customer delivery strategy, while remaining deeply involved in the work yourself. This is not a role for someone who wants to manage delivery from a distance. We expect you to understand our customers' problems, get into the technical details with your team, join critical customer conversations, and help solve the hardest deployments.

You'll be both the architect of the organization and an active participant in the work.

Get hands-on with our hardest deployments. Work directly with customers and your team on complex implementations. You'll be comfortable jumping into an architecture discussion, helping scope a deployment, troubleshooting an implementation, or joining an executive customer conversation when needed.

Build the playbook. Create repeatable frameworks for scoping, implementation, deployment, escalation, and handoff without forcing every customer into the same model.

Own the path from sale to production. Partner closely with Sales and Solutions Architects before contracts are signed to ensure we're setting customers and our own teams up for successful deployments.

Drive customer outcomes and success. Establish clear definitions of implementation success, time-to-value, deployment health, and customer outcomes, and build the systems needed to measure and improve them.

Make the organization more scalable. Identify where we should solve a problem through people, process, product, documentation, tooling, or automation. The goal isn't simply to add more Delivery headcount as customers grow.

title: Telemedicine Physician - Women's Hormone Expert - Remote (MD/DO only)
description:

Seeking Obstetrics/Gynecology, Internal Medicine, or Family Medicine physicians, and all other physicians with deep knowledge and experience in prescribing for midlife women’s healthcare. We are specifically looking for physicians who specialize in men's health and have experience prescribing testosterone and other hormone-boosting pharmaceuticals. Our services also include men’s hormone, weight loss and thyroid treatment and we would prefer to bring on physicians who have experience prescribing for patients in some or all of those categories as well. We are currently looking for physicians nationwide and highly value physicians who are licensed in multiple states.

We are a modern health company committed to giving our patients confidence as they age. Our goal is to help our patients break through highly stigmatized conditions using education and increasing access by making care more convenient and affordable. From initially only treating men who want to manage their testosterone levels, we have grown our services to support weight loss, thyroid treatments, and now women’s health. We are currently seeking part-time and full-time telemedicine physicians who want to be part of the health revolution. You will have the opportunity to leverage emerging technologies and provide digital telemedicine consultations to patients in the states in which you are licensed from the comfort of your home. We provide a training program and a supportive environment to help you improve your video consultation skills, including comprehensive technical support.
Your Responsibilities:

• Perform telemedicine consultations from our HIPAA-compliant video interface.

• Provide outstanding service and care to women in midlife navigating perimenopause, menopause, and other common midlife health challenges.

• Review lab results with patient and provide treatment options.

• Educate patients and create individualized treatment plans.

• Titrate medications based on patient outcomes.

• Prescribe medications if necessary based on your clinical diagnosis.

• Provide feedback to us to continually improve the patient experience.

• Available at a minimum of 6-8 hours/week for consultations, ideally 8-12 hours or more.

• You are an MD or DO who holds a valid license, ideally in multiple states.

• Minimum of 2 years of experience in Obstetrics/Gynecology, Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, and/or Hormone Replacement Therapy is preferred.

• NCMP (NAMS-certified menopause practitioner) certification is preferred.

• Possess an unrestricted DEA license and have prescribed Schedule III controlled substances.

• Excellent communication skills with a focus on physician-patient interaction.

• Comfortable with technology and video consultations, or the desire to learn.

• You are not just a pill pusher, but you have a deep profound care for hormone optimization.

• You are a self-starter who likes to be part of innovative mission-driven environments.

•
Minimum 5 years of experience in System Safety, Functional Safety, or Safety Risk Management within complex, safety-critical industries (such as autonomous vehicles, automotive, transportation, aerospace, aviation, robotics, defense, or medical devices).

Strong working knowledge of traditional hazard analysis and risk

If you're looking for a corporate HR job where you push paper all day this isn't it.

description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Maritime Digital Production (MDP) is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build and deploy the full technology stack that powers Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, the manufacturing execution system (ArsenalOS) that workers and planners use every shift, the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that eliminate manual toil from both the shop floor and business operations.

MDP operates at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology. Our systems live where factory-floor machines, edge compute, and OT networks meet enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure. We incubate solutions close to the production line, validate them with real operators building real hardware, harden them for reliability and security, and then scale them across multiple sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship.

This is not a support function. It is a strategic investment by Anduril in the premise that digitizing the manufacturing lifecycle end-to-end, from engineering definition through scheduling through execution through field feedback, is how Heavy Metal will out-build, out-adapt, and out-scale the traditional defense industrial base. MDP is scaling from a founding team to 70+ engineers across multiple U.S. sites. You will be joining early, working on hard problems with real operational stakes, and shaping how manufacturing software is built at Anduril from the ground up.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Senior Numerical Optimization Engineer on this unique initiative, you will own the scheduling optimization core that decides when and how ships get built. This project represents a shipyard's work as a graph of 100,000+ manufacturing operations carrying precedence, spatial, resource, and qualification constraints, then continuously replans as the factory changes. You will formulate that problem, build and benchmark the solvers that attack it, and keep them fast and trustworthy enough that a new plan can reach the floor within minutes of a disruption.

This is a research-grade problem with production consequences. Resource-constrained project scheduling at this scale is NP-hard, there is no ground truth to measure against, and a schedule has to be stable enough that the shop floor is not thrashed every time it changes. You will have the latitude to develop novel approaches and the obligation to ship them.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Formulate shipyard production scheduling as a mathematical optimization problem covering precedence with lag, disjunctive spatial exclusion, multi-resource capacity with qualification matching, calendars and shifts, and material availability.

• Own the solver-agnostic scheduling interface, integrate commercial and open-source solvers behind it, and benchmark them against each other on makespan, stability, resource utilization, and solve time.

• Build the two-tier replan path: fast local repair that returns a feasible schedule in seconds for a bounded affected subgraph, and background global re-so

Join CARED , a fast-growing health-tech startup. Own the operational front end of the participant journey, manage our referral inbox and make sure every referral moves quickly from enquiry through intake, matching and booking.

About CARED

CARED is a fast-growing healthcare technology startup helping people access allied health services faster and more easily.

We support NDIS participants across Occupational Therapy, Speech Therapy, Psychology, Neuropsychology, Physiotherapy, Exercise Physiology, Behaviour Support and Dietetics.

We already receive strong, qualified referral demand. As that demand grows, we are expanding our Service Navigation team to make sure every participant receives a prompt, thoughtful and well-coordinated journey into care.

About the role

As our Service Intake Lead, you will own the operational coordination of new referrals from the moment they arrive in the CARED inbox through to practitioner matching and booking.

This is not a traditional reception or phone-based intake role.

Incoming calls are answered by our professional reception service, while our Service Navigation Lead takes the lead on participant and referrer phone conversations where a more detailed discussion is required.

The Service Navigation Lead works directly with participants, families and Support Coordinators to understand their circumstances, determine which allied health services may be required and map the participant’s service requirements, including discipline, clinical needs, goals, modality, location, practitioner preferences, urgency and any barriers to commencing care.

As Service Intake Lead, you turn that information into action.

You will manage incoming referrals and the Service Navigation inbox, gather and document information, identify missing requirements, coordinate with the Service Navigation Lead, progress referrals through HubSpot, identify suitable practitioners and capacity, and coordinate appointment options and bookings in Cliniko.

You will primarily communicate with participants, families, Support Coordinators and other referrers via email and SMS, ensuring questions are answered, outstanding information is obtained and everyone knows what is happening next.

You’ll work closely with the Service Navigation Lead and Service Delivery Lead to make sure there is a seamless handover between understanding a participant’s needs, mapping their service requirements, matching them with the right practitioner and getting their services underway.

All roles maintain oversight of participants at Ready to Match and Matched stages so matching never becomes dependent on one person.

The standard is simple:

Every participant knows what is happening next. Every referral has an owner, a next action and a path towards care. Nothing goes quiet.

What you’ll do

Inbox and referral management

• Own and actively manage the Service Navigation inbox throughout the day.

• Review, triage and action new referrals and enquiries promptly.

• Ensure same-day acknowledgement and progression of new referrals wherever possible.

• Respond to participant, family, Support Coordinator, Plan Manager and referrer emails.

• Identify missing referral information and proactively follow it up.

• Ensure inbox enquiries are resolved, assigned or progressed rather than simply responded to.

• Maintain clear visibility of outstanding actions and follow-ups.

• Recognise urgent, complex, safeguarding, clinical, funding and Behaviour Support matters requiring escalation.

Intake and service mapping support

• Work closely with the Service Navigation Lead, who conducts phone-based intake conversations where required.

• Ensure information gathered during Service Navigation conversations is accurately captured in HubSpot and translated into clear service requirements.

This is a generalist role covering a broad range of topics: customer contracts, DPAs, corporate questions, data protection, employment matters, IP and copyright, and new technology regulation. You’ll sit in the Regulatory & Quality team but work with everyone at Flinn, from the founders to Sales, Product and People.

At Flinn, Legal isn’t here to list reasons why something can’t be done. Your job is to tell hard legal boundaries apart from risks we can manage, and to help the company find practical, lawful ways forward. When something isn’t possible, we want to hear how we could do it instead.

The Manager will oversee a small, specialized team of analysts focused on reporting, data quality, operational insights and resolution services team.

This role is responsible for executing the operational reporting strategy, including the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of recurring and as needed reports and insights. The Manager will leverage tools such as Power BI and internal systems, along with AI-enabled capabilities, to reduce manual data preparation, improve data accuracy, and increase automation across reporting processes.

The Manager will play a key role in monitoring performance trends across key performance indicators (KPIs) such as productivity, quality, SLA adherence, and operational effectiveness. This includes identifying data anomalies, highlighting risks, and delivering actionable recommendations to improve performance and reduce manual inefficiencies.

This position will also focus heavily on quality and control oversight and continuous improvement by establishing feedback loops, identifying root causes of errors, and driving improvements that enhance accuracy and reduce reliance on manual data entry processes.

Section 2: Job Functions, Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Manage the day-to-day execution of operational reporting, including daily, weekly, and monthly deliverables across productivity, quality, SLA, and performance metrics

• Oversee a small team of analysts responsible for reporting, analytics, and data quality support functions

• Ensure accuracy, consistency, and timeliness of all reporting outputs provided to leadership and business partners

• Execute and continuously improve automated reporting solutions using Power BI, internal tools, and AI-enabled capabilities

• Reduce reliance on manual data aggregation by identifying and implementing automation opportunities

• Monitor key performance indicators and identify trends, risks, and opportunities for operational improvement

• Provide clear, data-driven insights and recommendations to the Director and senior stakeholders

• Establish and maintain quality monitoring processes to ensure data accuracy and integrity across reporting

• Develop and maintain feedback loops to communicate performance results, quality issues, and improvement opportunities

• Identify and analyze root causes of data quality issues and partner with operations and technology teams to implement solutions

• Support SLA reporting and ensure accurate tracking and communication of performance

• Collaborate with cross-functional partners to enhance reporting capabilities, data quality, and system functionality

• Assist in forecasting, capacity planning, and analysis through accurate and timely reporting support

• Maintain documentation of reporting processes, methodologies, and controls

• Ensure adherence to policies, procedures, and controls and maintain compliance with regulatory requirements

• Communicate insights, trends, and recommendations in a clear and actionable manner

• Support continuous improvement initiatives focused on reducing manual data entry and improving efficiency

• Responsible for protecting, securing, and proper handling of all confidential data

• Demonstrate organizational values including I-Client Service philosophy and Core Values of People Matter, Quality First and Integrity Always®

Supervision

Dein Impact. Unsere Mission.

title: Procurement Manager
description:
About Us
Every moment of every day, people all over the world rely on the infrastructure work provided by Quanta Services and Quanta Government Solutions (QGS). With its highly skilled and innovative workforce, Quanta is the largest specialty contractor in North America that powers modern life. Find your future with us by being a part of something bigger - leading the energy transition in building a better world for generations to come.
Imagine what you could do here. We encourage and inspire our people to embrace opportunities within our corporate office and 200 operating companies providing solutions for the utility, renewable energy, electric power, industrial, communications and government industries worldwide.
Quanta’s culture is about creating an environment where all employees can be themselves, are valued, and have an equal opportunity to succeed. When you join our team, you join a dynamic culture in which career development is encouraged, excellence is rewarded, and diversity is valued.
About this Role
JOB TITLE: Procurement Manager
QUANTA COMPANY: Quanta Government Solutions, LLC
DEPARTMENT: Preconstruction and Proposal Operations
LOCATION: Remote with site travel
REPORTS TO: Director, Preconstruction Operations
CLASSIFICATION: Exempt
POSITION OVERVIEW:
We are seeking an experienced federal procurement leader to run day-to-day procurement for a growing federal EPC prime contractor. Working under the Director of Preconstruction and Proposal Operations, you will implement the QGS procurement policy and plan across our Energy and Department of War work and build a purchasing operation that holds up to government review. You will source and buy for pursuits and awarded projects. Every purchase file you touch should be ready for an auditor the day it closes.
What You'll Do

• Implement and run the QGS procurement policy, plan, and procedures under the Director’s leadership, and keep the written procedures current as regulations change.

• Lead sourcing for pursuits and awarded work: RFQs, competition, quote leveling, and documented price or cost analysis, including sole-source justifications when competition is not practical.

• Build and maintain purchase files that are audit-ready, covering competition, price reasonableness, source selection, exclusion checks in SAM, and consent to subcontract when the prime contract requires it.

• Make sure the right federal requirements and flowdowns reach every buy, including Buy American, Section 889, cybersecurity clauses where they apply, labor standards, and small business subcontracting plan goals and reporting.

• Maintain procurement integrity and conflict-of-interest controls, support mandatory disclosure reviews with Contracts and Legal, and apply pass-through charge limits to affiliate and lower-tier subcontracts.

• Obtain and review subcontractor cost or pricing data when the applicable threshold and contract require it.

• Apply the Director’s preferred-provider decisions between Quanta affiliate companies and external firms, and document price reasonableness for every affiliate buy to the same standard as an external buy.

• Maintain the qualified supplier and subcontractor list, prequalification, and performance scorecards.

• Plan material and long-lead procurement against the project schedule, and track commitments through delivery.

• Hand complete award packages to the Contracts Manager for drafting and the sourcing file to the Award Transition Project Manager, then own material and long-lead buyout from execution through delivery so awarded work starts fully bought out.

• Prepare for and support purchasing system reviews and customer audits, and run periodic self-audits of procurement files.

• Build and develop the procurement team as volume grows, participating in hiring with final decisions made by the Director.

What You'll Bring

• Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Construction Management, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

title: Accounting AI Research Contributor
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Aptura is looking for Subject Matter Experts from accounting and financial reporting, in practice or in-house, who build reporting packs, consolidations and reconciliations in Excel. You have used AI tools on your own work and been frustrated by the mistakes they make. You will turn that experience into realistic Excel tasks that test how well AI does the work of an Accountant.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Writing realistic Excel tasks drawn from your own work: extending existing models, fixing broken ones and building from a brief

- Working through each task yourself so there is a clear, correct answer

- Writing yes-or-no criteria precise enough that a grader can mark any attempt against them

NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS

- 3+ years in accounting, audit or financial reporting under IFRS or US GAAP, in practice or in-house

- Deep hands-on Excel: financial reporting, three-statement checks, purchase accounting, error tracing and pivot tables

- Strong written English communication skills.

- Attention to detail, and willingness to learn concepts in AI and Evals

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

- Start Date : Immediate

- Duration: Approximately 4-6 weeks

- Payment: task-based. Experts who complete their first task within the required timeline will then be qualified to do multiple tasks for the remainder of the project.

CONTRACT AND PAYMENT TERMS

- You will be engaged as an independent contractor.

- This is a fully remote role that can be completed on your own schedule.

- Projects can be extended, shortened, or concluded early depending on needs and performance.

- Your work at Aptura will not involve access to confidential or proprietary information from any employer, client, or institution.

- Payments will be weekly following task completion.

GETTING STARTED

- Apply with your details and CV. Choose an available 30-minute group walkthrough call.

- Attend the walkthrough and create one original task from your own work. Submit the brief, the actual input workbook(s) needed to complete it. Input-file uploads are compulsory.

- Write the brief yourself. Input workbooks must also be human-built. Use real data that has been sanitised, or public data with the source named. No AI usage allowed.

- We run your task against current frontier AI models. If the models get it wrong, you then write a detailed yes-or-no rubric, and a reviewer signs off on the task with you.

- Completing onboarding does not guarantee a job offer; selection remains subject to written approval of the task proposal.

ABOUT APTURA

Aptura is an applied AI and data company working with frontier labs to train AI systems on real professional work. We do this by building high-quality evaluation and training environments that teach AI agents to produce work that can be used in daily workflows.

title: Engineering Technician, Actuators
description:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role

We are seeking Engineering Technicians to support the assembly, testing, and prototyping of custom electromechanical actuators for advanced robotic systems. You will build and test hardware from engineering drawings and procedures through inspection, troubleshooting, and rework, partnering closely with mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, and test engineers.

These roles focus on hands-on work with precision electromechanical hardware, including stator prototypes, motor and actuator assemblies, and mechanical and electrical testing. You will help turn engineering designs into validated hardware while improving build records, work instructions, and repeatable assembly and test practices for future robotic platforms.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 5 days a week.

In this role, you will:

Each opening focuses on actuator builds, testing, or stator prototyping, with responsibilities aligned to the selected specialty.

- Actuator builds: assemble subassemblies and complete actuators from drawings, bills of materials, and work instructions, checking fit, orientation, torque, routing, and workmanship.

- Testing: set up and run established mechanical and electrical tests, confirm the setup against the procedure, record measurements, and identify unexpected results.

- Stator prototyping: support winding, insulation, termination, bonding, inspection, and rework using the selected build process and documented instructions.

- Troubleshoot build and test issues with engineers. Isolate problems through inspection and measurement, escalate deviations, and verify the result after approved rework.

- Maintain accurate build and test records, part and revision traceability, inspection results, and rework history.

- Use bench observations to improve work instructions, fixtures, tooling, and parts organization as prototypes evolve.

- Follow safety, ESD, cleanliness, and quality practices, and communicate material shortages, unclear instructions, and other blockers as priorities change.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have hands-on experience building or testing mechanical, electrical, or electromechanical hardware in a lab, prototype shop, or manufacturing environment.

- Can work from drawings, bills of materials, wiring diagrams, and procedures, and recognize when the instructions and hardware do not agree.

- Use hand tools, torque tools, and measurement equipment carefully, with consistent workmanship and attention to units and acceptance limits.

- Troubleshoot methodically, document observations, and know when to pause work and ask for engineering support.

- Take ownership of build quality and records while adapting to changing designs and priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience relevant to the selected specialty may include:

- Building or testing actuators, motors, robotics hardware, servos, or other precision electromechanical systems.

- Motor manufacturing, especially stator assembly, winding, insulation, termination, bonding, impregnation, or inspection.

- Soldering, crimping, connector assembly, harness routing, adhesives, or fixture-assisted assembly.

- Mechanical or electrical test setup, instrument checks, measurement capture, and documenting unexpected results.

- Inspection, traceability, nonconformance handling, and structured rework.

- Hands-on rework, basic machining, or prototype part modification using shop tools.

- Use of calipers, micrometers, multimeters, LCR meters, insulation-resistance testers, or torque tools.

title: Instructional Designer- Partner Specific
description:
This position is not open to applicants residing in or otherwise based in California, New York, Illinois, or Massachusetts. Additionally, applicants must be located in the Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific time zones.
Note to Applicants
We’re looking for professionals who take pride in their work. We know your resume tells part of the story, but our application questions help us understand how you think and work. Because we receive a high volume of applications, only applications with complete, thoughtful responses will be reviewed.

Given the AI restriction on this engagement, described below, we ask that your responses be your own work.
Engagement Details
This is instructional design work, with a twist.
Every project starts with an existing course and a charter that defines exactly what is changing about it. The work is reading that charter closely, translating it into specific revisions in specific places, and executing them cleanly on a short, fixed cycle, without drifting into the parts of the course the charter does not cover.
It calls on the full instructional design skill set: learning theory, alignment, assessment design, accessibility, and SME collaboration. What is distinctive is where the difficulty sits. The hard calls here are about scope and defensibility: deciding what a charter line means in practice, and documenting why you drew the line where you did. It also means finding things you would want to change and leaving them alone. If your instinct when you open a course is to fix everything you find, this engagement will frustrate you. If you can see all of it and still deliver only what the charter covers, documenting the rest for the partner, you should do well here.
You will work with Subject Matter Experts and coordinate with internal teams, including Editorial and Quality Review, ensuring every revision adheres to research-based practice and partner-defined quality standards.
This engagement carries a partner data restriction. No partner course content, materials, or partner-provided information may be entered into, uploaded to, or processed by any AI system, internal or external, at any point during the engagement.
This is an independent contractor engagement (1099). Contractors are free to work with other clients, and accepting one project carries no obligation to accept another. Meeting times are set in advance around each project’s milestones. Outside of those scheduled meetings and agreed deadlines, you determine your own working hours and process for completing the work.
Scope of Work

• Complete a scoped review of the assigned course and map the charter to specific course locations, documenting cascading effects, assumptions, and ambiguities before development begins.

• Deliver a specific list of items requiring SME input before the first working session.

• Collaborate with SMEs to revise instruction and assessments in scope, aligned to learning outcomes and the charter, while documenting anything outside scope rather than addressing it.

• Suggest relevant open educational resources and instructional methods appropriate to the revision.

• Maintain comprehensive documentation of design decisions to support partner review and approval.

• Incorporate partner and stakeholder feedback through agreed revision cycles.

• Facilitate SME working sessions to obtain the approvals required to complete deliverables.

• Coordinate with internal teams at defined handoff points to ensure deliverables are completed on schedule.

• Complete self-QA before each handoff and deliver complete, accurate work by each fixed milestone.

• Submit a status update with each milestone deliverable, and flag anything that's off track as soon as you identify it, so downstream stakeholders aren't caught by surprise.

• Work from the version of the design standards and charter in effect for your project. Both may be revised between projects as the program evolves.

What You Need to Get the Job Done

Who You Are
We're hiring a Product Designer, but we're not looking for someone who only designs screens. You're excellent at your craft, have strong product taste, and are comfortable stepping beyond traditional design boundaries when that's what the product needs.

• You have a high bar for what good looks like and care deeply about how products look, feel, and work.

Your Responsibilities

• Facilitate workshops to uncover problems and understand users to define what we are solving, why, and for whom.

• Conduct UX research, including user interviews, usability tests, surveys, competitive analyses, card sorts, literature reviews, UX audits, and heuristic evaluations.

• Distill research findings into actionable next steps and constraints for design.

• Explore solutions by architecting experiences using journey maps, story maps, site maps, flow diagrams, sketches, and low fidelity wireframes.

• Create UX and UI deliverables by designing medium and high fidelity wireframes.

• Demonstrate interactions and user flows by creating clickable/tappable prototypes.

• Align design decisions with client business goals and KPIs to drive business outcomes.

• Establish visual design guidelines by exploring typography, colors, logos, imagery, illustrations, and iconography.

• Prepare designs for handoff by creating robust and scalable atomic design systems, annotating wireframes, and supporting development requirements.

• Gather and iterate on client feedback directly, while maintaining clear communication and setting realistic expectations throughout the process.

• Optimize internal processes including design, client management, project management, and development by identifying areas of improvement and proposing solutions.

• Be comfortable using AI-assisted design and development workflows, including tools such as Paper.design and Claude Code, to explore, communicate, and iterate on solutions.

Keys to success

• Be comfortable with ambiguity. You will succeed if you are able to effectively digest information from clients, even when contradictory, distill what is truly important, and make thoughtful suggestions and adjustments.

• Be passionate about growth. You will succeed if you continuously look to improve your skills and level up the abilities of the team as a whole. We are big on giving and receiving feedback.

• Be thoughtful about defining and addressing problems. You will succeed if you dig deep to learn more about why problems exist and where their roots lie. We leverage research and workshops to dive into the problems we’re being asked to solve.

• Be practical with your solutions. You will succeed if you prioritize your tasks efficiently and know when it’s time for creativity versus when it’s time to deliver quickly.

title: Enterprise Account Manager (Strategic Renewals) - UK
description:
About Flosum

Every large company now runs critical parts of its business on Salesforce: sales, service, financial data, patient records, citizen services. When a release breaks something or data goes missing, revenue stops and regulators call. Flosum is the platform these companies trust to ship changes safely, protect their data, and recover fast.
We are in the middle of the most exciting chapter in our history. Our customers have relied on our Salesforce-native platform for years. Now we are bringing them a new cloud-native platform they can run on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or on-premises. We have also launched sandbox management built for the AI era, so teams can test AI agents such as Agentforce on production-ready environments in minutes instead of days.
Our customers include some of the most demanding enterprises in banking, insurance, healthcare, the public sector, and technology. They don’t buy us casually, and they don’t leave us casually. Your job is to make sure they never want to.

The role
You will own a book of enterprise accounts and one number: retained revenue. You decide which accounts need you most this week, and you go there. This is a commercial role. You will spend your time with executives, not running support tickets.

What you will do

• Own renewals across your book, from strategic accounts to smaller ones, and protect every dollar of recurring revenue.

• Build relationships with the executives who decide: CIOs, CTOs, VPs of Engineering, and heads of Salesforce platforms. Reach past your champion when the account needs it.

• Turn red accounts green. Spot risk early, build a save plan, and run it with urgency.

• Move customers from our Salesforce-native products to our cloud-native platform, and make the business case for why it matters to them.

• Defend your accounts against competitors, in-house builds, and new enterprise architectures.

• Pull the right people in. Hold product, support, engineering, and customer success accountable for what your customers need.

• Find expansion opportunities and hand them to our sales team with a clear plan.

• Run your book with discipline: accurate forecasts, clean renewal pipeline in Salesforce, no surprises.

Requirements
What you bring

• 7+ years in enterprise account management, renewals, or customer-facing sales at a B2B software company.

• You have carried a significant book of business (ideally $5M+ in annual recurring revenue) with individual accounts above $250K.

• You have sold or renewed complex IT solutions: DevOps, data protection, security, infrastructure, or developer platforms. Technical buyers trust you.

• A track record of saving at-risk renewals by going to the executive level, with the numbers to prove it.

• Commercial intensity. You negotiate well, you push for multi-year terms, and you are comfortable with hard conversations about price and value.

• You know how NRR and GRR are calculated and how your work moves them.

• Clear, concise writing and speaking. You can brief a CIO in five minutes.

• Experience in the Salesforce ecosystem is a strong plus.

Benefits

Why join now

• You will work with customers at the moment they move to the cloud. Few account managers get to shape a transition this large.

• Our products sit in the path of AI adoption. Every company deploying AI agents on Salesforce needs to test, release, and protect them safely.

• You will have real ownership, direct access to leadership, and the room to build how account management works here.

• Competitive base plus variable compensation tied to retention.

Reporting directly to the CFO, and with a growth path to Controller, you'll be responsible for major portions of the accounting close, financial reporting, technical accounting, audit process, and accounting infrastructure. • Own significant portions of the monthly, quarterly, and annual close, ensuring accuracy and full compliance with US GAAP.

• Work closely with the CFO and finance leadership on accounting-related initiatives and broader finance priorities.

What You Bring

• Deep working knowledge of US GAAP, with 5-7+ years of experience in SaaS or usage-based revenue businesses, including revenue recognition complexity under ASC 606.

• Direct experience with multi-entity financial reporting and consolidation.

• A track record of evaluating and deploying ERP or accounting systems, and genuine fluency with AI tools as part of your everyday accounting workflow.

description:

Location: Remote - Canada

Like WCG, you believe in the power of work. As a Labour Market Information (LMI) Specialist , you’ll be responsible for the collection, research, analysis, and effective dissemination of labour market information, research, and policies internally and to WCG's external collaborators to support the organization's operational performance and growth.
What you'll do

• Collect, understand, analyze and interpret labour market information on a national, provincial and community level that provides value to various internal and external collaborators in our company (e.g., for operational performance, business development, marketing, and strategic planning)

• A bachelor's degree (Masters preferred) in social sciences, economics, business administration or in a related discipline and/or combination of equivalent relevant education and experience

• Strong written communication skills including ability to produce exceptional written content for a range of audiences within tight deadlines

• Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and adapt to constant change

• Administrative support as required

• Must successfully pass a Criminal Record Check

• Competitive salary of $ 70,000 - $ 80,000 per year (based on full-time hours)

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!
